title: Update: I added Orcs to my isometric character creator. The Goblins weren't enough trouble, apparently.
author: TheSpriteWizard
selftext:
Hey everyone! It's The Sprite Wizard again.

Some of you might remember [SpriteForge](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/spriteforge), the isometric character creator I've been working on to help indie devs make consistent pixel-art characters without having to draw hundreds of frames.

Well, I've been busy in the tower.

**Update 0.4.0 is here, and the Orcs have arrived!**

The Goblins apparently weren't enough trouble, so I've added **male and female Orcs**, complete with nine skin tones, their own lore, and nearly the entire wardrobe and armoury refitted for their considerably larger bodies.

That's three customizable species now: Humans, Goblins, and Orcs.

And because I apparently enjoy making more work for myself, I've also given the Grimoire a pretty substantial makeover.

**Here's what's new:**

* **Orcs!** Male and female bodies with nine skin tones and hundreds of clothing and equipment options.
* **A redesigned interface.** Ornate bronze frames, new navigation tabs, equipment shortcuts, and a magical compass that lets you rotate your character.
* **Better equipment fitting.** Helmets, armour, boots, and clothing now fit different body types much more naturally.
* **More customization controls.** Adjust the size and positioning of weapons, shields, backpacks, helmets, and other accessories.
* **Consistent character positioning.** No more characters jumping around the preview while you're changing equipment.

And, of course, we still have **71 animations, up to 16 rendering directions, and more character combinations than I have any business trying to calculate.**

Last time I counted, we were somewhere north of 50 octillion.

That was before the Goblins and Orcs.

I'm not counting again.

**No generative AI is used in the tool.** It's built around customizable 3D characters and a pixel-art rendering engine, so you can create consistent characters and animations for your games.

As before, **the browser version is free to use**, and there's a downloadable Windows version for anyone who wants to support development and get the additional export functionality.

[**Try SpriteForge here!**](https://thespritewizard.itch.io/spriteforge)

I'm still actively working on it, and there's plenty more coming. Dwarves, Elves, Zombies, and mounts are all waiting for their turn in the Grimoire.

If you give it a try, I'd appreciate hearing what you think. Bug reports, suggestions, complaints about my questionable fashion choices. All welcome.

Thanks again to everyone who's been trying out my tools and helping me improve them. It's been pretty cool seeing people actually use this stuff to make their games.

Anyway, back to the tower. I've got three female Orc outfits that still need fitting, and the Grimoire won't stop complaining about them.

**— The Sprite Wizard**
